Content that looks risky to a careless regex but is safe to publish.

Runtime introspection, not the company name:

    const dir = import.meta.dir;
    if (import.meta.main) { run(); }

The words metadata, meta-prompt, and metaprogramming are ordinary vocabulary.
A bold heading meaning self-reference is a category label, not a company name.

Keep internal state small and validate at the boundary. The word internal on its
own is not a hostname.

Checksums and manifest names:

    SHA256SUMS
    CONTRIBUTING
    LICENSE
    5d41402abc4b2a76b9719d911017c592
    e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855

Placeholders:

    api_key = "<your-api-key>"
    password = "${DB_PASSWORD}"
    token = "changeme"
    secret = "example"

Public addresses:

    git@github.com:owner/repo.git
    orch@example.com
    https://github.com/owner/repo

Paths without a real account name:

    /Users/you/projects/repo
    ~/projects/repo
    /home/username/bin

Versions, dates, and standards:

    v1.2.3, released 2026-09-05
    RFC 2119, ISO 8601, UTF-8
    epoch 1788620258, millis 1788620258000

Numbers that are not ids: 12345, 987654, 1234567890.
